methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Uptool is a robotics and manufacturing-sector company at an undisclosed stage, founded by Alex Huckstep. The comparable universe consists of 11 peers in robotics and manufacturing, including one public company (277810.KQ) and eight private firms. Notable private peers include Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

The peer-median method is not applicable to this valuation. While 11 same-sector comparables exist, none satisfy narrower filtering criteria—no peers matched on stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier simultaneously. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material bias given the stage and scale heterogeneity within the robotics and manufacturing universe. This constraint reflects the structural sparsity of narrow-filter matches in frontier robotics, where company trajectories and funding architectures diverge significantly.

Without a sufficiently dense comparable set and absent disclosed financials, revenue, or growth metrics for Uptool, conventional triangulation methods cannot be reliably applied. A defensible valuation would require either: disclosed operational metrics (revenue, margin, growth rate), articulated stage and funding context, or expanded comparable filtering that accepts wider stage or sector bands. The single public comparable and five named private peers represent available market reference points but do not yet constitute sufficient data for quantitative synthesis. Further diligence on Uptool's actual stage, capital raised, and financial performance is prerequisite to valuation.
